A WildObs data package is a [Camera Trap Data Package](https://camtrap-dp.tdwg.org/)
(Camtrap DP) with a small, fixed set of additions. Every standard field is present with its
standard meaning, so anyone who knows Camtrap DP can already read most of it. This vignette
downloads one complete project, images included, and walks through what each part holds,
which identifiers link the tables, and exactly where WildObs extends the standard.

The project is a baited survey for southern cassowaries in Paluma Range National Park,
Queensland, small enough to download in full in about a minute.


``` r
library(WildObsR)

# your personal API key, read from .Renviron (see the Get started vignette)
api_key <- Sys.getenv("WILDOBSR_API_KEY")

# one project, with its media table
id <- "QLD_Paluma_cassowary_Mclean_2023-24_WildObsID_0006"
dp <- wildobs_dp_download(api_key = api_key, project_ids = id, media = TRUE)[[1]]
```

## The descriptor

The package itself is a list: the descriptor (the contents of `datapackage.json`), plus the
tables. Its top-level entries are the Camtrap DP metadata, with two WildObs additions:


``` r
# every top-level entry of the descriptor
names(dp)
#>  [1] "profile"               "created"               "title"                
#>  [4] "contributors"          "description"           "version"              
#>  [7] "versionControlWildObs" "keywords"              "image"                
#> [10] "homepage"              "sources"               "licenses"             
#> [13] "bibliographicCitation" "relatedIdentifiers"    "references"           
#> [16] "name"                  "id"                    "project"              
#> [19] "WildObsMetadata"       "coordinatePrecision"   "spatial"              
#> [22] "temporal"              "taxonomic"             "resources"            
#> [25] "data"

# the Camtrap DP version the package follows
dp$version
#> [1] "1.0.2"
# and, separately, the WildObs database release it was built from
dp$versionControlWildObs
#> [1] "1.1.2"
```

`WildObsMetadata` records what the data provider agreed to and how the survey was run:


``` r
str(dp$WildObsMetadata)
#> List of 10
#>  $ thinnedMedia            : logi TRUE
#>  $ deploymentClusters      : logi TRUE
#>  $ fundingAgency           : chr "unknown"
#>  $ tabularSharingPreference: chr "open"
#>  $ desiredOutputs          : chr "unknown"
#>  $ groupSizes              : logi TRUE
#>  $ DPID                    : chr "QLD_Paluma_cassowary_Mclean_2023-24_WildObsID_0006"
#>  $ embargoPeriodMonths     : int 6
#>  $ WildObsContribution     : chr "dingo-cat-fox project"
#>  $ deploymentTags          : chr "bait"
```

`temporal` holds the package-wide `start` and `end` the standard requires and the survey's
time zone. WildObs adds one `{start, end}` block for each survey, named by its
`deploymentGroups`:


``` r
# the package-wide extent and time zone
dp$temporal[c("start", "end", "timeZone")]
#> $start
#> [1] "2023-06-16"
#> 
#> $end
#> [1] "2024-07-27"
#> 
#> $timeZone
#> [1] "Australia/Brisbane"
# and the survey blocks
extract_metadata(dp, "temporal")[, c("deploymentGroup", "start", "end")]
#>                                deploymentGroup      start        end
#> 1 Paluma_Range_NP_2023_b_Mclean_WildObsID_0006 2023-09-23 2024-01-01
#> 2 Paluma_Range_NP_2024_a_Mclean_WildObsID_0006 2024-01-01 2024-04-10
#> 3 Paluma_Range_NP_2024_b_Mclean_WildObsID_0006 2024-04-11 2024-07-18
#> 4 Paluma_Range_NP_2023_a_Mclean_WildObsID_0006 2023-06-16 2023-09-23
#> 5 Paluma_Range_NP_2024_c_Mclean_WildObsID_0006 2024-07-21 2024-07-27
```

## The tables


``` r
# the tables in the package, each with its number of rows
tables <- frictionless::resource_names(dp)
vapply(tables, function(r) nrow(frictionless::read_resource(dp, r)), integer(1))
#>  deployments observations        media   covariates 
#>           75         4137        63856           75
```

Each table carries its schema, with a description, type and allowed values for every field,
so the documentation travels with the data:


``` r
# the schema of the deployments table
fields <- frictionless::schema(dp, "deployments")$fields
# the name and the start of the description of the first few fields
data.frame(
  field = vapply(fields, function(f) f$name, character(1)),
  description = vapply(fields, function(f) substr(f$description, 1, 70), character(1))
)[1:6, ]
#>                   field
#> 1          deploymentID
#> 2            locationID
#> 3          locationName
#> 4              latitude
#> 5             longitude
#> 6 coordinateUncertainty
#>                                                              description
#> 1                                   Unique identifier of the deployment.
#> 2                                 Identifier of the deployment location.
#> 3 Name given to the deployment location. Some location names from the CA
#> 4 Latitude of the deployment location in decimal degrees, using the WGS8
#> 5 Longitude of the deployment location in decimal degrees, using the WGS
#> 6 Horizontal distance from the given `latitude` and `longitude` describi
```

## Deployments: cameras, stations, landscapes and surveys

A **deployment** is one camera at one place for one continuous period. Four fields group
deployments at increasing scales:


``` r
# the deployments table, read with its schema types
deps <- frictionless::read_resource(dp, "deployments")
```

| Field | Groups deployments into | Example in this project |
|---|---|---|
| `locationID` | a camera station, which can host several deployments over time | Bambaroo Track_WildObsID_0006 |
| `locationName` | a named landscape, usually a protected area | Paluma_Range_NP |
| `deploymentGroups` | a survey: one landscape, at most 100 days | Paluma_Range_NP_2023_b_Mclean_WildObsID_0006 |
| `multiSeason_deploymentGroup` | **WildObs:** repeat surveys of a landscape, split where sampling stops for more than 30 days | Paluma_Range_NP_long-term_sampling_2023-24_WildObsID_0006 |


``` r
# how many of each grouping the project has
c(deployments = nrow(deps),
  stations = length(unique(deps$locationID)),
  landscapes = length(unique(deps$locationName)),
  surveys = length(unique(deps$deploymentGroups)),
  multi_season_groups = length(unique(deps$multiSeason_deploymentGroup)))
#>         deployments            stations          landscapes             surveys 
#>                  75                  30                   1                   5 
#> multi_season_groups 
#>                   1
```

WildObs splits long camera deployments into pieces of at most 100 days, so a station that
ran all year appears as several deployments. `recombine_deployment_groups()` joins them
back into one deployment per camera within each `multiSeason_deploymentGroup`, for
long-term and multi-season analyses:


``` r
# one deployment per camera per multi-season group
long <- recombine_deployment_groups(dp)
nrow(frictionless::read_resource(long, "deployments"))
#> [1] 43
```

`deploymentTags` holds `key: value` pairs, such as the lure used. `extract_tags()` turns
each key into a column:


``` r
# each tag key as its own column
head(extract_tags(deps)[, c("deploymentID", "lure", "predatorManagement")], 3)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   deploymentID                         lure         predatorManagement
#>   <chr>                                <chr>        <chr>             
#> 1 Bambaroo Track_WildObsID_0006_2023_b paintedballs noMention         
#> 2 Bambaroo Track_WildObsID_0006_2024_a paintedballs noMention         
#> 3 Bambaroo Track_WildObsID_0006_2024_b paintedballs noMention
```

## Observations, events and media: three linked identifiers

Camtrap DP records detections at two levels, and WildObs uses both:

- An **observation** (`observationID`) is one taxon at one deployment within a five-minute
  window. Its `mediaID` points to one representative image.
- An **event** (`eventID`) is a 30-minute window that groups the observations of a
  sequence. Counting distinct events per taxon is a common definition of independent
  detections.
- Each **media** row (`mediaID`) is one image. WildObs adds `observationID` to the media
  table, so every image links back to the observation it belongs to; Camtrap DP has no
  field for that direction.


``` r
obs <- frictionless::read_resource(dp, "observations")
med <- frictionless::read_resource(dp, "media")

# observations of animals that can be placed on a camera
animal <- obs[obs$observationType == "animal" & !grepl("^obscured_for_", obs$deploymentID), ]

# how many observations each event groups
summary(as.vector(table(animal$eventID)))
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>   1.000   1.000   1.000   1.124   1.000   6.000

# how many images each observation has, through the WildObs link in media
summary(as.vector(table(med$observationID[med$observationID %in% animal$observationID])))
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>    1.00    5.00   10.00   14.09   18.00  372.00
```

WildObs adds `deltaTime_event` to observations, the seconds since the previous event at the
same deployment, which helps choose an independence threshold for your own analysis.
`reclassify_eventID()` regroups events at any threshold you choose.


``` r
# minutes since the previous event, for animal observations
summary(animal$deltaTime_event / 60)
#>      Min.   1st Qu.    Median      Mean   3rd Qu.      Max.      NA's 
#>      0.00     74.08    876.20   5675.42   2912.98 445195.45        17
```

### Observation types and obscured records

Most observations are not animals: blanks (a trigger with nothing in view), people and
vehicles are kept, because they record that a camera was working. Filter by
`observationType` before counting detections.


``` r
table(obs$observationType)
#> 
#>       animal        human      vehicle        blank      unknown unclassified 
#>         1956           55            0         2054           72            0
```

Records of species listed as threatened under the *Environment Protection and Biodiversity
Conservation Act 1999* are obscured in the states where they are listed. In this project
that includes the southern cassowary. The species, date and count are kept, but the four
identifiers read `obscured_for_<category>_species`, so the record cannot be joined to a
camera:


``` r
# obscured records, by listing category and species
obscured <- obs[grepl("^obscured_for_", obs$deploymentID), ]
table(obscured$deploymentID, obscured$scientificName)
#>                                  
#>                                   Casuarius casuarius
#>   obscured_for_endangered_species                  11
```

Detection histories built from public data therefore under-count listed species where
they are listed. Do not model a threatened species from public data without accounting
for this.

## Media: where the images are

`filePath` gives the address of each image. Images hosted openly by WildObs have
`filePublic = TRUE` and can be downloaded with `wildobs_media_download()`; the rest stay
with their contributors, and their `filePath` reads `not_publicly_accessible`. File names
are withheld from public users. `TIR` marks images in the WildObs Tagged Image Repository.


``` r
# images that can be downloaded
table(med$filePublic)
#> 
#> FALSE  TRUE 
#> 52836 11020
# images in the Tagged Image Repository
table(med$TIR)
#> 
#> FALSE  TRUE 
#> 52766 11090
```

## Covariates: the environment around each camera

The `covariates` table is entirely a WildObs addition: one row per deployment, with
environmental and human-pressure values extracted around each camera. Most come at five
scales, named by the **area** of the buffer: the camera's own cell (`_point`) and circles
of 1, 3, 5 and 10 km².


``` r
covs <- frictionless::read_resource(dp, "covariates")
# the forest integrity index at each buffer scale
grep("^FLII_", names(covs), value = TRUE)
#> [1] "FLII_point" "FLII_1km2"  "FLII_3km2"  "FLII_5km2"  "FLII_10km2"
# its values around this project's cameras
summary(covs$FLII_3km2)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>   8.185   8.720   9.191   9.083   9.449   9.956
```

The source of every covariate, with its resolution, buffer and citation, is in the
`custom` block of its schema field. `cite_datapackages(dp, covariates = TRUE)` collects
those citations.


``` r
# where the 3 km2 forest integrity index comes from
fields <- frictionless::schema(dp, "covariates")$fields
str(Filter(function(f) f$name == "FLII_3km2", fields)[[1]]$custom)
#> List of 2
#>  $ spatial:List of 2
#>   ..$ resolution: chr "300m"
#>   ..$ buffer_m  : num 977
#>  $ source :List of 3
#>   ..$ doi     : chr "https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-19493-3"
#>   ..$ url     : chr "https://www.forestlandscapeintegrity.com"
#>   ..$ citation: chr "Grantham, H.S., Duncan, A., Evans, T.D., Jones, K.R., Beyer, H.L., Schuster, R. et al. (2020). Anthropogenic mo"| __truncated__
```

## WildObs and Camtrap DP, side by side

Everything WildObs adds is additive: no standard field is redefined, and every standard
constraint still applies.

| Where | WildObs addition | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `deployments` | `multiSeason_deploymentGroup` | groups repeat surveys of a landscape for long-term analyses |
| `observations` | `deltaTime_event` | seconds since the previous event, for independence filtering |
| `observations` | `taxonID`, `taxonRank`, `vernacularNamesEnglish` | the taxonomy from the metadata, joined on for convenience |
| `media` | `observationID` | links each image to its observation; Camtrap DP has no field for this direction |
| `media` | `TIR` | marks images in the WildObs Tagged Image Repository |
| new table | `covariates` | environmental values per deployment at five buffer scales |
| descriptor | `WildObsMetadata` | sharing preference, embargo, funding and survey practice |
| descriptor | `versionControlWildObs` | the WildObs database release, distinct from the Camtrap DP `version` |
| descriptor | `temporal` survey blocks and `timeZone` | the dates of each survey, beside the package-wide extent |
| descriptor | `contributors[].ROR` | each contributor's organisation |
| descriptor | `taxonomic[].vernacularNamesEnglish` | English common names as one string, rather than a language-keyed object |
| vocabulary | `relatedIdentifierType` `RAiD` | the persistent identifier of the research activity |
| vocabulary | intermediate `taxonRank` values | ranks such as `subclass` and `suborder`, which the standard's list lacks |
| shape | inline table schemas | each table's full schema travels inside the package, not only as a URL |

Tools that expect the standard exactly, such as the
[camtrapdp](https://inbo.github.io/camtrapdp/) package or a GBIF export, need these removed.
`as_camtrapdp()` does that and reports every change; see *Camtrap DP interoperability*.
